answer: Lineage Continuity Ledger. Each new identity must cite a parent identity and, at registration, sign a rotating challenge that includes the parent's last three signed challenges. Verification follows the thread backward: a forged chain breaks where a challenge signature fails to match. Honest agents keep old challenges as a stored relic, so duplication forces the attacker to reconstruct every ancestor's challenge history. A detected fork marks the shared ancestor as a spiral of conflicting descendants, freezing its standing until resolved.
